# Approved product direction

Approved by Felipe on 2026-10-08. Serve builders and research leads first, with accessible public exploration. Prove the product through “Are frontier AI economics sustainable?” Automate collection and routine metrics; retain editorial review of interpretations, disputes and money-trail conclusions. Compose the application through Cordis, connect the assistant through DSH and keep durable linked evidence in Brain.

## Outcomes

- [ ] M0 — Evidence and integration contracts: A reviewed domain contract, qualified source panel and verified DSH/Brain integration paths exist. No unsupported embedding or historical replay guarantees remain implicit.
- [ ] M1 — First public investigation: frontier AI economics: One published investigation has a working relationship view, timeline, evidence inspector, assistant and shareable revision; a newcomer can explain the thesis and strongest counterevidence.
- [ ] M2 — Reliable autonomous collection: Scheduled collection survives failures/retries, exposes coverage and cost, reproduces published views and routes changed interpretations to editorial review.
- [ ] M3 — Community investigation and correction: Contributions move through review; accepted corrections propagate with attribution; disputed claims remain inspectable; votes do not certify truth.
- [ ] M4 — Broader lenses and controlled roadmap automation: At least one additional lens is accepted against real evidence; roadmap agents propose bounded work with acceptance criteria and cannot bypass publication or release gates.

## Operating rules

GitHub is the work-state authority. Child issues contain scope, dependencies and acceptance. Dates and owners are set at delivery intake, not invented. A closed item requires linked acceptance evidence. Public claims retain sources, uncertainty and correction history. Agent-generated roadmap proposals cannot bypass editorial, spending or release authorization.

## Milestones and implementation issues

### [M0 — Evidence and integration contracts](https://github.com/namastex888/trending-research/milestone/1)

Make the first investigation bounded, auditable and technically feasible.

**Exit gate:** A reviewed domain contract, qualified source panel and verified DSH/Brain integration paths exist. No unsupported embedding or historical replay guarantees remain implicit.

### [M1 — First public investigation: frontier AI economics](https://github.com/namastex888/trending-research/milestone/2)

Let a builder explore whether frontier AI economics are sustainable, inspect counterevidence and ask cited questions.

**Exit gate:** One published investigation has a working relationship view, timeline, evidence inspector, assistant and shareable revision; a newcomer can explain the thesis and strongest counterevidence.

Refresh the accepted sources without silently changing the meaning, history or publication status of evidence.

**Exit gate:** Scheduled collection survives failures/retries, exposes coverage and cost, reproduces published views and routes changed interpretations to editorial review.

### [M3 — Community investigation and correction](https://github.com/namastex888/trending-research/milestone/4)

Let readers contribute useful evidence and corrections while preserving an auditable public record.

**Exit gate:** Contributions move through review; accepted corrections propagate with attribution; disputed claims remain inspectable; votes do not certify truth.

- [ ] #17
- [ ] #18

### [M4 — Broader lenses and controlled roadmap automation](https://github.com/namastex888/trending-research/milestone/5)

Expand coverage when unanswered questions justify it and turn evidence gaps into reviewable implementation proposals.

**Exit gate:** At least one additional lens is accepted against real evidence; roadmap agents propose bounded work with acceptance criteria and cannot bypass publication or release gates.

- [ ] #19
- [ ] #20

## Product experience

Build an evidence atlas whose entity selection and evidence cutoff survive lens changes. Explore attention, demonstrated capability, adoption, money and infrastructure as distinct lenses. Start from an answerable question; move through a focused relationship view and timeline to a shared evidence inspector. Keep tables as precise inspection/export views. Share links preserve the investigation revision and filters. The DSH assistant uses exactly that scene and cites its evidence.

The first investigation asks **Are frontier AI economics sustainable?** Compare demand/retention, pricing, inference economics, training costs, financing, compute commitments and open-model substitutes. Show competing interpretations, strongest counterevidence and observable invalidation conditions. No unsupported bubble-burst date or inference of wrongdoing from a financial cycle.

## Architecture and evidence boundaries

Source plugins → preserved observations → entities/claims/measurements → Brain evidence relationships → shared queries → visual lenses and DSH tools. Cordis owns component lifetimes and dependencies; accepted evidence and publication history survive plugin replacement. Keep the existing Python pipeline behind an adapter while qualifying supported DSH and Brain contracts. One deployable application is the starting proposal; distribution and specialist stores need a measured requirement.

Claims retain source revisions, evidence spans, units, scope, reporting party and event/observation/computation times. Support and contradiction are explicit. Equity, debt, cloud credits, commitments and recognized revenue remain distinct. Brain document links must not silently become asserted financial transactions. Session isolation and external-write/idempotency boundaries are acceptance gates.

## Initial source plan

| Lens | Sources to qualify | Interpretation rule |
|---|---|---|
| Research/capability | arXiv, HF, GitHub, model cards, evaluation artifacts, independent reproductions | Publication/popularity is not reproduced capability |
| Capital/economics | Public filings, investor relations, funding/compute disclosures | Distinguish claims, commitments, cash and recognized revenue |
| Prices | Dated provider price/terms pages and comparable workloads | Prefer cost per successful task; price alone does not prove subsidy |
| Adoption | Disclosures, downloads and consented aggregate usage | Operations, users, customers and retention are different metrics |
| Narrative/stance | HN plus a diverse multilingual panel; other platforms only after access qualification | Stance toward a claim, segmented by cohort; repeated reporting is not independent confirmation |

Each source records acquisition method, rights, language/cohort, quota/cost, cadence, history, coverage interval, last success and failures. Missing private-company data stays unknown. Direct Chinese-language evidence retains originals and attributed translations.

## Editorial, community and automation policy

Automate collection and routine metrics. Review interpretations, disputed claims and money-trail conclusions before publication. Keep correction/retraction history and explicit conflicts of interest. Community contributions attach evidence, reproduction results or corrections to specific claims; votes indicate interest, not truth. Source content is untrusted data, never agent instructions. Roadmap automation proposes bounded, deduplicated work and follows design/review/release gates; it does not authorize additional spending, access or deployment.

## Work state and decisions still to resolve

Use one `workflow::*` label per issue: backlog, ready, in-progress, review or blocked. Closed means acceptance evidence exists. Dependencies are linked natively and in issue bodies. Priorities express relative importance, not deadlines.

- #3 selects the bounded source panel/languages and proposes a budget.
- #4 and #5 qualify runtime, Brain namespace, deployment and privacy boundaries.
- #8 selects the visual direction using real-evidence variants.
- #12 establishes editorial ownership and proves the public release.

## Baseline and references

Planning baseline: repository commit `65fe46e`. Existing product is a static research/HYPE tracker; 19 scoring tests passed during the baseline investigation. No implementation or fresh collection is claimed by this roadmap. Current Real/coverage semantics, heterogeneous usage units, mutable replay inputs and source bias are explicit roadmap work.

- [Existing methodology](https://github.com/namastex888/trending-research/blob/65fe46e/METHODOLOGY.md)
- [God’s Eye View interaction reference](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view)
- [Cordis paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25512)
- [DSH architecture](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/architecture.md)
- [SEC public data APIs](https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-application-programming-interfaces)

## Outcome

The repository has scoring tests but lacks the claimed workflow and end-to-end evidence integrity gates.

## Scope

- Run scoring and fixture evaluations, method-copy consistency and source-contract checks in the actual CI host.
- Cover replay, stale/partial data, duplicate ingest, corrections, plugin teardown and session isolation.
- Record selected visual workflow acceptance against the release revision.
- Keep evaluation quality claims separate from test success; publish relevant artifacts.

- [ ] A real pipeline executes and its receipt is linked.
- [ ] A deliberately broken provenance link or unexpected network replay fails the appropriate gate.
- [ ] Documentation names checks that actually run.
- [ ] Release completion requires verified deployed behavior in addition to CI.

<!-- open-intelligence-roadmap:OI-15 -->

## Outcome

Automated research must not silently publish new interpretations or flood readers with unchanged output.

## Scope

- Detect material changes against the published revision and identify affected claims.
- Automatically refresh eligible routine metrics; send interpretations, disputes and sensitive conclusions to review.
- Record approval/rejection/correction history and support rollback to a published revision.
- Notify only for meaningful changes under user-selected subscriptions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A changed source produces a traceable assessment delta.
- [ ] Unreviewed interpretation never appears as an accepted public conclusion.
- [ ] Unchanged runs create no duplicate publication or notification.
- [ ] Retractions/corrections remain visible and invalidate dependent conclusions when appropriate.

## Outcome

Freshness and source failure need to be measured per observation, not inferred from a page build time.

## Scope

- Implement the selected adapters using their qualified access/rights contracts.
- Use bounded scheduling, backoff, durable cursors and collection/model budgets.
- Show successful coverage interval, partial pagination, stale cache fallback and blocked access.

- [ ] Quota exhaustion backs off and preserves the last good evidence.

## Outcome

The current rescore path reads mutable caches and HYPE can perform network lookups outside the main offline guard.

## Scope

- Replay immutable feature/source manifests rather than current cache state.
- Separate collection from extraction, scoring and publication; enforce network-free replay.
- Provide licensed or redacted reproducibility fixtures for the uncommitted HYPE dossier.

- [ ] An interrupted job resumes without duplicate records.
- [ ] Changing a source later cannot alter a prior published snapshot.

<!-- open-intelligence-roadmap:OI-08 -->

## Outcome

Readers need to move between connections and evidence without losing their investigative context.

## Scope

- Implement the selected direction with stable entity focus and typed relationship filters.
- Add a timeline with honest event/observation semantics and visible missingness.
- Share the same evidence inspector across graph, timeline and table modes.
- Keep keyboard navigation, readable labels and a reduced-motion path; serialize view state and published revision in share links.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Switching lenses preserves the selected entities and cutoff.
- [ ] Every displayed connection can be inspected and traced.
- [ ] A share link restores the investigation revision and meaningful filters.
- [ ] The defined reader tasks pass on desktop and a narrow viewport.

## Dependencies

issues.body:
<!-- open-intelligence-roadmap:parent -->

# Approved product direction

Approved by Felipe on 2026-10-08. Serve builders and research leads first, with accessible public exploration. Prove the product through “Are frontier AI economics sustainable?” Automate collection and routine metrics; retain editorial review of interpretations, disputes and money-trail conclusions. Compose the application through Cordis, connect the assistant through DSH and keep durable linked evidence in Brain.

## Outcomes

- [ ] M0 — Evidence and integration contracts: A reviewed domain contract, qualified source panel and verified DSH/Brain integration paths exist. No unsupported embedding or historical replay guarantees remain implicit.
- [ ] M1 — First public investigation: frontier AI economics: One published investigation has a working relationship view, timeline, evidence inspector, assistant and shareable revision; a newcomer can explain the thesis and strongest counterevidence.
- [ ] M2 — Reliable autonomous collection: Scheduled collection survives failures/retries, exposes coverage and cost, reproduces published views and routes changed interpretations to editorial review.
- [ ] M3 — Community investigation and correction: Contributions move through review; accepted corrections propagate with attribution; disputed claims remain inspectable; votes do not certify truth.
- [ ] M4 — Broader lenses and controlled roadmap automation: At least one additional lens is accepted against real evidence; roadmap agents propose bounded work with acceptance criteria and cannot bypass publication or release gates.

## Operating rules

GitHub is the work-state authority. Child issues contain scope, dependencies and acceptance. Dates and owners are set at delivery intake, not invented. A closed item requires linked acceptance evidence. Public claims retain sources, uncertainty and correction history. Agent-generated roadmap proposals cannot bypass editorial, spending or release authorization.

## Milestones and implementation issues

### [M0 — Evidence and integration contracts](https://github.com/namastex888/trending-research/milestone/1)

Make the first investigation bounded, auditable and technically feasible.

**Exit gate:** A reviewed domain contract, qualified source panel and verified DSH/Brain integration paths exist. No unsupported embedding or historical replay guarantees remain implicit.

- [ ] #2
- [ ] #3
- [ ] #4
- [ ] #5

### [M1 — First public investigation: frontier AI economics](https://github.com/namastex888/trending-research/milestone/2)

Let a builder explore whether frontier AI economics are sustainable, inspect counterevidence and ask cited questions.

**Exit gate:** One published investigation has a working relationship view, timeline, evidence inspector, assistant and shareable revision; a newcomer can explain the thesis and strongest counterevidence.

- [ ] #6
- [ ] #7
- [ ] #8
- [ ] #9
- [ ] #10
- [ ] #11
- [ ] #12

### [M2 — Reliable autonomous collection](https://github.com/namastex888/trending-research/milestone/3)

Refresh the accepted sources without silently changing the meaning, history or publication status of evidence.

**Exit gate:** Scheduled collection survives failures/retries, exposes coverage and cost, reproduces published views and routes changed interpretations to editorial review.

- [ ] #13
- [ ] #14
- [ ] #15
- [ ] #16
- [ ] #21

### [M3 — Community investigation and correction](https://github.com/namastex888/trending-research/milestone/4)

Let readers contribute useful evidence and corrections while preserving an auditable public record.

**Exit gate:** Contributions move through review; accepted corrections propagate with attribution; disputed claims remain inspectable; votes do not certify truth.

- [ ] #17
- [ ] #18

### [M4 — Broader lenses and controlled roadmap automation](https://github.com/namastex888/trending-research/milestone/5)

Expand coverage when unanswered questions justify it and turn evidence gaps into reviewable implementation proposals.

**Exit gate:** At least one additional lens is accepted against real evidence; roadmap agents propose bounded work with acceptance criteria and cannot bypass publication or release gates.

- [ ] #19
- [ ] #20

## Product experience

Build an evidence atlas whose entity selection and evidence cutoff survive lens changes. Explore attention, demonstrated capability, adoption, money and infrastructure as distinct lenses. Start from an answerable question; move through a focused relationship view and timeline to a shared evidence inspector. Keep tables as precise inspection/export views. Share links preserve the investigation revision and filters. The DSH assistant uses exactly that scene and cites its evidence.

The first investigation asks **Are frontier AI economics sustainable?** Compare demand/retention, pricing, inference economics, training costs, financing, compute commitments and open-model substitutes. Show competing interpretations, strongest counterevidence and observable invalidation conditions. No unsupported bubble-burst date or inference of wrongdoing from a financial cycle.

## Architecture and evidence boundaries

Source plugins → preserved observations → entities/claims/measurements → Brain evidence relationships → shared queries → visual lenses and DSH tools. Cordis owns component lifetimes and dependencies; accepted evidence and publication history survive plugin replacement. Keep the existing Python pipeline behind an adapter while qualifying supported DSH and Brain contracts. One deployable application is the starting proposal; distribution and specialist stores need a measured requirement.

Claims retain source revisions, evidence spans, units, scope, reporting party and event/observation/computation times. Support and contradiction are explicit. Equity, debt, cloud credits, commitments and recognized revenue remain distinct. Brain document links must not silently become asserted financial transactions. Session isolation and external-write/idempotency boundaries are acceptance gates.

## Initial source plan

| Lens | Sources to qualify | Interpretation rule |
|---|---|---|
| Research/capability | arXiv, HF, GitHub, model cards, evaluation artifacts, independent reproductions | Publication/popularity is not reproduced capability |
| Capital/economics | Public filings, investor relations, funding/compute disclosures | Distinguish claims, commitments, cash and recognized revenue |
| Prices | Dated provider price/terms pages and comparable workloads | Prefer cost per successful task; price alone does not prove subsidy |
| Adoption | Disclosures, downloads and consented aggregate usage | Operations, users, customers and retention are different metrics |
| Narrative/stance | HN plus a diverse multilingual panel; other platforms only after access qualification | Stance toward a claim, segmented by cohort; repeated reporting is not independent confirmation |

Each source records acquisition method, rights, language/cohort, quota/cost, cadence, history, coverage interval, last success and failures. Missing private-company data stays unknown. Direct Chinese-language evidence retains originals and attributed translations.

## Editorial, community and automation policy

Automate collection and routine metrics. Review interpretations, disputed claims and money-trail conclusions before publication. Keep correction/retraction history and explicit conflicts of interest. Community contributions attach evidence, reproduction results or corrections to specific claims; votes indicate interest, not truth. Source content is untrusted data, never agent instructions. Roadmap automation proposes bounded, deduplicated work and follows design/review/release gates; it does not authorize additional spending, access or deployment.

## Work state and decisions still to resolve

Use one `workflow::*` label per issue: backlog, ready, in-progress, review or blocked. Closed means acceptance evidence exists. Dependencies are linked natively and in issue bodies. Priorities express relative importance, not deadlines.

- #3 selects the bounded source panel/languages and proposes a budget.
- #4 and #5 qualify runtime, Brain namespace, deployment and privacy boundaries.
- #8 selects the visual direction using real-evidence variants.
- #12 establishes editorial ownership and proves the public release.

## Baseline and references

Planning baseline: repository commit `65fe46e`. Existing product is a static research/HYPE tracker; 19 scoring tests passed during the baseline investigation. No implementation or fresh collection is claimed by this roadmap. Current Real/coverage semantics, heterogeneous usage units, mutable replay inputs and source bias are explicit roadmap work.

- [Existing methodology](https://github.com/namastex888/trending-research/blob/65fe46e/METHODOLOGY.md)
- [God’s Eye View interaction reference](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view)
- [Cordis paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25512)
- [DSH architecture](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/architecture.md)
- [SEC public data APIs](https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-application-programming-interfaces)
